# Dot / dumbbell / lollipop

Contents: [Use cases](#use-cases), [Chart IDs](#chart-ids), [Minimal spec](#minimal-spec), [Data](#data), [Options](#options), [Annotations](#annotations), [Sizing](#sizing), [Fixtures](#fixtures).

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-reference.mjs from the boardplot describe, list and fixtures payloads. -->

Position-encoded item comparison — Cleveland dots, dumbbell ranges with derived gaps, or lollipops. Type `dot`. Aliases: `cleveland`, `dumbbell`, `lollipop`.

## Use cases

- Gap between two values
- Many items on one scale
- Before and after per item

## Chart IDs

- `dot.dot`: fixture `dot-range-benchmark`
- `dot.dumbbell`: fixture `share-shift-dumbbell`
- `dot.lollipop`: fixture `audit-findings-lollipop`

## Minimal spec

```json
{
  "type": "dot",
  "data": {
    "categories": [{ "id": "north", "label": "North" }, { "id": "south", "label": "South" }],
    "series": [{ "id": "revenue", "label": "Revenue", "values": [120, 90] }]
  },
  "options": { "unit": "$k", "title": "North revenue exceeds South by $30k", "source": "Illustrative data" }
}
```

## Data

A `cell` is a number, null or a value object; see [Value cell](options.md#value-cell).

| Path | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| valueKind | string |  | Default valueKind for all series. One of `'fraction'`. |
| categories | array | yes | Categories defining the dot-chart rows. |
| categories[].id | string | yes | Category identity used to match keyed values and annotation anchors. |
| categories[].label | string |  | Displayed category name; defaults to the category id and supports line breaks. A date id or `date` without a label prints a short date such as '4 Sep'. |
| categories[].date | string |  | ISO 8601 date associated with the category. |
| categories[].footnote | integer |  | 1-based reference into options.footnotes. The number is drawn beside this category label as the reference mark, and the note it points at keeps that number; a reference to no note draws nothing and warns, and notes the engine derives print unnumbered. |
| series | array | yes | Values and optional ranges to compare across each category row. |
| series[].valueKind | string |  | Multiply numbers by 100 into pct cells; explicit pct cells stay in percent units. One of `'fraction'`. |
| series[].id | string | yes | Series identity used by keyed options, annotations and legend entries. |
| series[].label | string |  | Displayed series name; defaults to the series id. |
| series[].values | (cell \| { categoryId, value: cell })[] | yes | Values in category order, or keyed entries pairing a categoryId with its value. |
| series[].scenario | string |  | AC, PY, PL, FC (or ACT, BUD, FCST). |
| series[].direction | string |  | Declared preference for higher or lower values in directional comparisons. One of `'higherIsBetter'`, `'lowerIsBetter'`. |
| series[].role | string |  | Declares a plotted data series or a comparison reference series. One of `'data'`, `'reference'`. |
| series[].colorRole | string |  | Theme color role used for this series when no explicit fill takes precedence. One of good, bad, warn, neutral, neutralLight, highlight, total, others; series-N for step N of the theme ramp, 1-based (series-2 is color.series[1]); or status-<key> for a theme status colour. A hex colour goes in fill. |
| series[].fill | string |  | Explicit CSS fill color for this series; remains authored across theme changes. |
| series[].unit | string |  | Unit of this series' values. Without a format example, a $k, $m, k or m unit prints its labels whole from 100 up, in place of options.unit. |
| series[].format | string |  | Format-by-example for this series' labels, for example 1,234 or 1.2%. Overrides options.format; a cell format overrides it. |

## Options

| Path | Type | Values | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| legend | string \| object | `'top'`, `'bottom'`, `'none'`, `'auto'` (or another value of its type) |  | Key position. Multiple series get a key by default unless visible direct labels name them. 'none' hides the key; unnamed series warn. |
| axisTitles | object |  |  | Title of the value axis when it is drawn: under the value-axis tick row, ending at the right edge of the plot. Drawn only when authored. |
| axisTitles.primary | string |  |  | 'Measure, unit' title of the value axis, e.g. 'Margin, %'. |
| variant | string | `'dot'`, `'dumbbell'`, `'lollipop'` | `'dot'` | Dot by default; dumbbell joins paired values and lollipop joins values to the baseline. |
| averageMarker | boolean \| object |  |  | Computed dashed average rule with a solver-placed Ø label, as on bar and column: the mean of every dot of the series in scope ('all' by default, or the listed series). |
| averageMarker.scope | string \| array | `'all'` (or another value of its type) |  | Series included in the computed average; defaults to 'all'. |
| arrow | boolean |  |  | Dumbbell only (warning arrow-dumbbell-only otherwise): an arrowhead at the second series' dot shows the direction of change. The connector is painted good or bad by the sign of the change when the second series declares direction, neutral otherwise; a pair whose dots nearly touch keeps a plain connector. |
| gapColumn | boolean |  |  | Dumbbell only: prints the gap, second series minus first, signed in a column right of the plot under a head such as 'Gap, pp' (pp for percent values). A highlighted row prints bold. Default false. The column stays off below 576 px canvas width. |
| methodNote | boolean |  |  | Default false. true adds the method footnote that names the marker inside a range as its supplied mid-point. A supplied range.mid is drawn and keyed either way. |
| range | object |  |  | What the drawn ranges are: their key entry and, on request, their bounds as numbers. |
| range.label | string |  |  | The key entry for the drawn ranges, naming the interval, for example 'Peer range, min to max' or 'Interquartile range'. Default 'Range'. |
| range.values | boolean |  |  | Default false. true prints each range's low and high value beside its caps. |
| range.midLabel | string |  |  | The key entry for the open marker that draws each supplied range.mid, for example 'Peer midpoint'. Default 'Midpoint'. When only some rows carry a mid, a note names the others. |

Plus the [shared options](options.md). This type does not accept `categoryLabels`, `valueAxis.tickStep`, `valueAxis.log`, `valueAxis.reverse`, `valueAxis.break`, `categoryAxis`, `secondaryAxis`, `topN`, `hatchStrength`, `colorblindSafe`, `rounding`.

## Annotations

An annotation anchor is a category or item id string, or an object with categoryId plus optional seriesId, segmentId and edge (start, end, total); pointId addresses a scatter point. Category anchors, including from/to, take category ids, not category labels.

| Kind | Purpose | Required | Anchors | Optional fields | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| valueLine | Draws a reference line at an authored value or an engine-computed mean, with optional tolerance shading and attainment fill between the line and resolved actuals. |  | from: categoryId (optional); to: categoryId (optional) | value: number \| 'mean', default mean. A number draws the line there; mean has the engine compute it. valueKind: 'fraction'. Multiply a numeric value and its tolerance by 100 before layout: 0.35 draws at 35%. Independent of data.valueKind. Omit it for values already in percent points; not valid with mean. label: string \| false. Name plus value; ${value} sets its position. A number already in the name is kept once. false hides it. | No anchor is required. Value defaults to mean. Scoped means are line-only: seriesId and paired from/to compute a primary-axis mean and limit its stroke to those bands; other types refuse scope fields for a mean. Numeric values cannot use scope fields except as a category clip with tolerance or attainment. A secondary-axis line needs an acknowledged secondary scale and an explicit numeric value. Optional tolerance shades a value-axis band; optional attainment fills between the line and resolved actuals. |
| callout | Places authored free text at an anchored data element, routing a leader when displaced and honoring the preferred side. | at, text | at: AnchorRef | preferSide: left \| right \| above \| below. Side the solver tries first; the label keeps a leader when it moves. headline: string. A bold first line over the text, which then prints in plain type; ${value} in it prints the anchored value from the data. Example: "headline": "${value}", "text": "Peak in handheld-loom demand" prints 153 in bold over the words. arrow: boolean, default false. A thin arrow from the text to the anchored point; the first line sits level with the point, right or left of it, where there is room. Not with icon or status. Example: "arrow": true. |  |
| note | Places authored text at an anchored data element through collision avoidance, with an optional icon or status chip. | at, text | at: AnchorRef |  |  |
| delta | Computes the signed difference between an anchored value and another anchor or literal, then places a collision-managed label at the first anchor. | at, vs | at: AnchorRef; vs: AnchorRef \| number |  |  |
| abs | Reads the anchored data value and places its formatted absolute value in a collision-managed label. | at | at: AnchorRef |  |  |
| diff | Draws a level-difference arrow between two anchors and computes either percent change or their signed value difference. | from, to | from: AnchorRef; to: AnchorRef | mode: relative \| absolute \| reversed, default relative. relative prints the percent change from 'from' to 'to', reversed the change from 'to' to 'from', absolute the value difference. | Mode defaults to relative. Relative and reversed changes need a nonzero base; negative bases use its absolute magnitude and emit a warning. Absolute mode reports the raw value difference. A hidden label removes its arm. The arm follows the horizontal value axis and clears the connector. |
| cagr | Draws a growth arrow between two anchored points and computes the compound annual growth rate from their values and ISO-date span. |  | from: AnchorRef (optional); to: AnchorRef (optional) | suffix: string, default 'p.a.'. Text after the rate. period: boolean. Print the period before the rate from the anchors' category labels, '2014–2019: +5.8% p.a.'. Default true when the chart carries two or more CAGRs, so nested brackets are told apart by their text, false otherwise. An arrow's ends show its span, so an arrow prints the rate alone unless period is true. shape: bracket \| arrow, default bracket. arrow draws one straight arrow over the marks with the rate in an oval on it, lifted until it clears them. Where no straight line clears the chart, the span is too short for the oval, a stack's inner layer is the anchor or the chart lays comparisons out itself, it draws the bracket and warns cagr-arrow-no-room. | Omitted endpoints span the first to the last category, or the first to the last total on a waterfall. Resolved endpoints need a positive date interval from ISO dates or year-bearing labels and a positive start value; an end of zero reads -100%, and a start at or below zero or a negative end omits the rate and warns cagr-undefined. On a continuous time axis the years are the exact span between the two readings. An anchor on one series of several (seriesId, or a line category, which reads the first drawn series) names that series in the label, "Product B +10.1% p.a.", and the arm runs from that series' segment or point. In text, ${value} prints the rate with its suffix, so "CAGR 2014–2019: ${value}" keeps the computed number. |

## Sizing

Floor 480 × 270 px; fit `fill`.
Below 480 px wide or 270 px high, down to the compact floor of 280 × 240 px, the chart draws in compact mode; `belowMinimum: 'refuse'` refuses there instead.

Below the floor a render is refused with `size-below-floor` and the pixels it needs. `measure` returns the natural and comfortable size for a given spec; see [Sizing in the manual](../manual.md#sizing).
